subject: health
unitTitle: Body Systems, Hygiene, and Disease Prevention
title: Correction and reflection: medication and poison safety
essentialQuestion: How can understanding body systems, hygiene, and disease prevention help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Medicines should be used only as directed by a responsible adult or qualified professional; unknown substances and household poisons should not be touched, tasted, or shared.
Classify urgency from observable facts, protect scene safety, activate trained help, and stay within current training rather than attempting an unsafe rescue.
For medication and poison safety, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Design an age-appropriate prevention routine and explain when adult help is required.
studentTask: Read three supplied fictional situations about medication and poison safety. For each, mark routine, urgent, or emergency; list the first safe action, the trained help to contact, and one action a bystander should avoid. Support each classification with a fact from the lesson.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in medication and poison safety; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the medication and poison safety task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
